headline: Alaska governor orders probe of Peltola campaign
summary: Gov. Mike Dunleavy ordered an investigation into whether Mary Peltola's Senate campaign helped recruit a second candidate named Dan Sullivan. Peltola called the reporting a distraction from the issues in the race.

headline: CNN polls: Democrats ahead in Texas and Michigan, close in Maine and Kansas
summary: New CNN polls of likely voters show Talarico leading Paxton 49%-43% in Texas and El-Sayed ahead of Rogers 49%-42% in Michigan. Jackson leads Collins 49%-45% in Maine and Hamilton leads Marshall 49%-45% in Kansas, both within the margin of error.

headline: Fox Power Rankings: South Carolina to toss-up, Ohio leans D
summary: Fox News moved South Carolina's Senate race to toss-up and shifted the Ohio Senate and governor races to Lean Democrat. It also moved 19 House races toward Democrats and projects them winning at least 223 seats, with Senate control still unresolved.

headline: No organized campaign backs Prop A map
summary: Prop A opponents have reported $5.4 million in large contributions since mid-September, while the main pro-map group says there is no organized effort to pass it. A yes vote keeps the 2025 congressional map for 2028 and later.

headline: Missouri clergy split over Amendment 3
summary: The state's Catholic bishops and the Missouri Baptist Convention back Amendment 3, which would repeal the 2024 abortion-rights amendment. About 90 clergy members signed a letter opposing it.

headline: Murkowski endorses Democrat for Alaska governor
summary: Republican Sen. Lisa Murkowski endorsed Democrat Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins in Alaska's race for governor.

headline: Pappas and Sununu clash in New Hampshire Senate debate
summary: Democratic Rep. Chris Pappas and Republican John E. Sununu sparred over the Iran war, tariffs and Social Security. Sununu, who has Trump's endorsement, has distanced himself from some of Trump's policies.

headline: Marist: Hochul leads Blakeman by 11 in New York
summary: Gov. Kathy Hochul leads Republican Bruce Blakeman 53%-42% among likely voters. Democrats lead the generic congressional ballot in New York 56%-42%.

headline: Suffolk/USA Today poll: Acton and Brown lead narrowly in Ohio
summary: Democrat Amy Acton leads Vivek Ramaswamy 48%-44% for governor, down from a 9-point lead in September. Sherrod Brown leads Sen. Jon Husted 47%-44% in the Senate race (500 likely voters, ±4.4 points).

headline: Clinicians group backs Amendment 3, but opponents count more signers
summary: The Missouri Clinicians Coalition held a news conference with physicians supporting Amendment 3 and says 75 providers have signed its pledge. A Stop the Ban Missouri letter urging a no vote had about 470 health care provider signers.

headline: Four GOP-held Pennsylvania House seats in play
summary: Inquirer/NYT/Siena polling shows Democrats narrowly ahead of Rep. Brian Fitzpatrick in PA-1 and Rep. Rob Bresnahan in PA-8, and tied with Rep. Scott Perry in PA-10. Democrat Bob Brooks has led Rep. Ryan Mackenzie for months in PA-7, the state's second-costliest House race.

headline: GOP poll: Ramaswamy's ad about Acton's mother is backfiring
summary: A private poll for a Republican group (800 likely Ohio voters, Oct. 23-26) found Democrat Amy Acton leading Vivek Ramaswamy 50%-42%, up from 2 points earlier in the month. Among voters aware of the $4 million ad featuring Acton's estranged mother, twice as many said it made them more likely to back Acton than less likely.

headline: El-Sayed's Michigan Senate lead grows to 7
summary: A Mitchell Research poll of 636 likely voters (Oct. 26-27) found Democrat Abdul El-Sayed at 51% and Republican Mike Rogers at 44%, up from a 4-point lead on Oct. 1. El-Sayed led independents 52%-38%, and 28% of respondents said they had already voted or were voting absentee.

headline: NYT/Siena: South Carolina Senate race tied at 48%
summary: A New York Times/Siena poll of likely voters found Democrat Annie Andrews and Republican Sen. Graham tied at 48% in South Carolina. In Florida, Sen. Ashley Moody led Democrat Angie Nixon 50%-44%, and in Minnesota, Democrat Peggy Flanagan led Republican Michele Tafoya 54%-40%.

headline: Judge rejects DOJ bid to set aside 20,000 California ballots
summary: U.S. District Judge David Carter denied the Justice Department's emergency request to make California segregate about 20,000 mail ballots from voters the administration labeled likely noncitizens. Carter wrote that the federal government had never before tried on the eve of an election to force a state to abandon its own election procedures.

headline: Report ties Peltola campaign to second Dan Sullivan; Trump urges prosecution
summary: A New York Times report, based partly on interviews with a fired former campaign manager and texts, said Mary Peltola's campaign appeared to help recruit the namesake candidate on Alaska's Senate ballot; Peltola's campaign and the DSCC deny involvement. Trump called for Peltola to be prosecuted, while legal experts said the report is unlikely to affect the DOJ certification lawsuit.

headline: Amendment 7 would create fund aimed at ending state taxes
summary: Amendment 7 would set up a 'Show-Me Prosperity Fund,' invested in S&P 500 index funds, with the goal of eventually replacing Missouri's income and sales taxes. The Missouri Budget Project estimates the fund would need about $609 billion in principal, and critics point to a projected $1.7 billion state deficit.

headline: Nevada refuses federal request to check voters with SAVE
summary: Secretary of State Cisco Aguilar said Nevada will not run its voter rolls through the federal SAVE citizenship database, citing too many false positives. The system has wrongly flagged hundreds of citizens in Missouri and dozens in Texas.

headline: Nearly 4.5 million Texans vote in first week of early voting
summary: About 23.4% of a record 19 million registered Texas voters had cast ballots through Sunday, slightly behind 2018's pace. Voters with a Democratic primary history made up 35% of early voters versus 33% for Republican primary voters; early voting ends Friday.

headline: Speaker Johnson to campaign for Nunn in Iowa
summary: House Speaker Mike Johnson plans to appear Wednesday in Urbandale for Rep. Zach Nunn, who faces Democrat Sarah Trone Garriott in a race Cook rates Lean Democrat.

headline: Amendment 3 backers pitch it as a middle path
summary: The measure would repeal the 2024 abortion-rights amendment with exceptions for rape and incest up to 12 weeks and for emergencies, and write the ban on gender-transition care for minors into the constitution. Sponsor Rep. Ed Lewis calls it moderate; opponents say it overturns voters' 2024 decision.

headline: Midterm ad spending sets an all-time record
summary: AdImpact counted $11.21 billion in ad spending and reservations for the 2025-26 cycle as of Monday night, edging past the $11.20 billion spent in the entire 2023-24 presidential cycle.

headline: Trump ties accepting results to 'honest' elections
summary: Asked on his way to Texas whether he would respect the midterm outcome, Trump said he would if the elections are honest. He also signaled he could work with Democrats if Republicans lose Congress, pointing to his veto power.

headline: How Prop A's map would redraw mid-Missouri
summary: A yes vote on Proposition A approves the 2025 congressional map, likely 7 Republican seats to 1 Democratic, while a no vote keeps the 2022 map. The 2025 map would stretch Kansas City's 5th District east to Jefferson City, Sedalia and Moberly and put all of Columbia in the 3rd District.

headline: Wagner makes her case in tightening 2nd District race
summary: Republican Rep. Ann Wagner, seeking an eighth term, faces Democrat Fred Wellman in Missouri's 2nd District as polls show a tightening race amid national Democratic momentum. Wagner has run ads attacking Wellman's past podcast remarks and finances; his campaign says he is current on his taxes.

headline: Benson leads James by about 7 in Michigan governor poll
summary: A Glengariff Group poll for WDIV and The Detroit News (Oct. 19–22, 600 likely voters) found Democrat Jocelyn Benson at 51.4% and Republican John James at 44.5%. About 4% were undecided.

headline: Marist: Jackson edges Collins; Maine governor race tied
summary: A Marist poll taken Oct. 22–25 found Democrat Troy Jackson at 49% and Sen. Susan Collins at 47% among likely Maine voters. In the governor's race, Democrat Hannah Pingree and Republican Bobby Charles were tied at 44%, with independent Rick Bennett at 6%.

headline: Trump returns to Texas as Paxton–Talarico race stays tied
summary: A new Fox News poll shows Republican Ken Paxton and Democrat James Talarico tied at 49% among likely Texas voters, after Talarico led 51%-49% last month. Trump is holding rallies Tuesday in Corpus Christi and Lubbock, his fourth Texas visit since Labor Day.

headline: Final PBS/NPR/Marist poll: Democrats lead generic ballot by 8
summary: The last PBS News/NPR/Marist poll before Election Day (Oct. 19–20) found likely voters favoring Democrats for Congress 52% to 44%, slightly narrower than last month among registered voters. Trump's approval stood at 40% among likely voters, and those who have already voted favored Democrats 68% to 31%.

headline: DOJ asks Washington to hold ballots of 400 voters
summary: The Justice Department asked Washington state to set aside any ballots cast by more than 400 people it suspects may not be citizens until their eligibility is confirmed. Secretary of State Steve Hobbs said he would respond only to requests that follow due process.

headline: Democrats lead Nevada early vote by about 24,000
summary: About 439,000 Nevadans, roughly 21% of active voters, had voted by Monday night. Democrats led by 24,395 ballots (5.5 points), powered by a 12-point edge in Clark County.

headline: Five super PACs top $1 billion in midterm spending
summary: An AFP analysis of federal data found five outside groups had spent more than $1 billion as of Oct. 25, nearly a third of all non-party spending this cycle, with about two-thirds benefiting Republicans. Elon Musk has put almost $450 million into GOP groups.

headline: Trump rallies in Mississippi for Hyde-Smith
summary: Trump held a rally at Corinth's Crossroads Arena to boost Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith and Rep. Trent Kelly, the first visit by a sitting president to the city since FDR. Democratic Senate nominee Scott Colom held a news conference in Corinth beforehand criticizing both Republicans.

headline: Texas Senate is the costliest race of the midterms
summary: Citing AdImpact, Newsmax reported the Texas Senate race has drawn about $500 million in ads and reservations, the most of any 2026 contest. AdImpact moved Ohio and Maine's Senate races to toss-up and projects California's governor race at a record $351 million.

headline: Appeals court won't order California to set aside 20,000 ballots
summary: A divided 9th Circuit panel declined the Justice Department's request to make California segregate about 20,000 mail ballots from people the administration suspects are noncitizens, saying it lacked jurisdiction at this stage. The case returns to a district court, which scheduled a hearing for Tuesday afternoon.

headline: Redrawn GOP districts turn into costly toss-ups
summary: Several seats Republicans redrew to favor themselves, including North Carolina's 1st District with over $42 million in ads, are now competitive. Two redrawn Florida districts are nearing $90 million in combined ad spending.

headline: Democratic super PAC spends in Trump-won House seats
summary: House Majority PAC spent about $2.2 million against Rep. Brad Finstad in Minnesota's 1st District and about $380,000 against Rep. Victoria Spartz in Indiana's 5th. GOP groups have shifted money among other House districts.

headline: Early vote passes 30 million a week before Election Day
summary: More than 30 million Americans had voted early as of Oct. 26, per the University of Florida Election Lab. Early turnout is running well above 2022 in Texas, Maine and Ohio but slightly below it in Iowa.

headline: DGA adds $5 million for Bottoms in Georgia
summary: The Democratic Governors Association put another $5 million into Keisha Lance Bottoms's campaign, on top of $11.5 million earlier. Republican Rick Jackson leads by single digits in polling averages in a race Cook rates a toss-up.

headline: Tariffs weigh on Republicans in the final stretch
summary: GOP candidates are defending Trump's tariffs while seeking relief from parts that hurt their states, and the White House exempted some Canadian goods after pressure from Sen. Susan Collins. Recent Pew and AP-NORC polling shows waning confidence in the tariffs.
